name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans R+12, a steep structural advantage for the incumbent party
Weber holds a roughly 30-to-1 fundraising and cash-on-hand edge over Bartie
Prediction markets price the Democratic win chance near 2 percent
No polls or expert ratings; incumbent seeking re-election with no outside opposition spending
model.rationale: An R+12 district, an incumbent with a roughly thirty-to-one money advantage, and markets pricing the Democrat's chances near two percent all point to a comfortable Weber hold; Bartie's campaign lacks the resources to make the race competitive.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a wave of outside spending behind Bartie would prompt a rethink.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 14th District, anchored in the Beaumont area and parts of the Gulf Coast, leans Republican by about twelve points. Randy Weber, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. His campaign has raised roughly $1.08 million and holds about $900,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Thurman Bartie has raised under $40,000 with about $5,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Weber.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Weber roughly a 96 to 98 percent chance of winning. The combination of a strongly Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced challenger makes this one of the least competitive House races on the ballot. Absent an unexpected development, Weber is well positioned to return for another term.
